author: cmungall
body: This trEMBL entry has no official GO annotations https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/A0A8B6BFL6/entry There are unofficial ProtNLM2 annotations that seem reasonable: I was surprised there were no GO annotations, because the domains seem well characterized: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/protein/UniProt/A0A8B6BFL6/entry/InterPro/#table E.g Reverse transcriptase (RNA-dependent DNA polymerase) https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/entry/pfam/PF00078/ All of the interpros are mapped to ECs: * IPR000477 [RT_dom](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/entry/InterPro/IPR000477/) [Reverse transcriptase domain](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/entry/InterPro/IPR000477/) * IPR043128 [Rev_trsase/Diguanyl_cyclase](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/entry/InterPro/IPR043128/) [Reverse transcriptase/Diguanylate cyclase domain](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/entry/InterPro/IPR043128/) * IPR043502 [DNA/RNA_pol_sf](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/entry/InterPro/IPR043502/) [DNA/RNA polymerase superfamily](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/entry/InterPro/IPR043502/) * IPR052055 [Hepadnavirus_pol/RT](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/entry/InterPro/IPR052055/) [Hepadnavirus polymerase/reverse transcriptase](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/entry/InterPro/IPR052055/) Those same ECs are consistently mapped to GO terms like RNA-directed DNA polymerase activity Logic dictates that if an EC is equivalent to a GO, then a mapping to an EC propagates to a GO. I suggest we start with this, and we can selectively remove mappings that are incorrect (removing the ipr2ec too). As an aside, this makes evaluating the ProtNLM annotations harder, because the ProtNLM set includes a lot of long-tail trembls like this, it seems it is making novel correct predictions; which technically it is, but only because of a bookkeeping error on our side.
title: Automatically chain ec2go and interpro2ec into interpro2go (Reverse transcriptase example)

author: sjm41
body:
Tagging InterPro folk - @sarach06 @blazaropinto @tony787 

I have asked them previously about the meaning/source of the EC numbers that appear on some InterPro entries - I think the answer was that they are simply the EC numbers that have been annotated to SwissProt entries that have the given InterPro domain. That is, there is not an "interpo2EC mapping" per se. But I'll defer to the InterPro curators to confirm/deny this!

author: sarach06
body:
Hi Steven,
Yes, that's correct. EC numbers are added to InterPro entries, automatically, there is not manually checked mapping and adding to them. We do sometimes mention or add EC numbers in the abstracts, but not always. Hope this helps, let us know if you have further questions or if there is anything we can do/change/improve.
Thanks!
Sara
